pages.title: Namadicus Elephant
pages.text: The Namadicus elephant ($(o)Palaeoloxodon namadicus$()) is an extinct elephant that lived on the Indian subcontinent during the Middle and Late Pleistocene.$(br2)It is named after the Narmada River valley in India, where its fossils were first found.$(br2)A close relative of the straight-tusked elephant of Europe, it shared that species' huge size and prominent bony crest at the top of the skull, and is regarded as one of the largest proboscideans ever.
